prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: 2024年重点信息化项目执行情况汇总表 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "项目" · longest unbreakable word 25px · one-line width 243px
  col 2: header "负责人" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 53px
  col 3: header "预算（万元）" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 104px
  col 4: header "进度" · longest unbreakable word 54px · one-line width 422px
  col 5: header "风险说明" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 2070px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 506px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 505px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"poor","why":"风险说明 is squeezed to roughly a third of the width (~6 characters per line), so the long risk paragraphs explode vertically and the whole table runs to ~3666px; 项目 still wraps to three lines, and the narrow 进度 column also fragments, so the sacrificed space buys nothing."},"B":{"grade":"poor","why":"负责人 is only ~40px wide, so names stack one character per line (李/建/国) and the header itself breaks vertically; 项目 breaks at ~3 characters per line. 风险说明 gets a fair share, but the identifier and header damage is severe."},"C":{"grade":"good","why":"负责人 names and 预算 figures stay on one line, 项目 wraps to a readable 3 lines, and 风险说明 takes the largest share, giving the shortest table of the set; only 预算（万元） wraps in the header and 进度 is a bit tight."},"D":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Cleanest hierarchy: 预算（万元） and 负责人 headers each sit on one line, names and amounts are intact, 风险说明 is clearly the dominant reading column, and 项目/进度 are given just enough room; near-shortest overall height with no column starved."},"E":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"风险说明 is generously wide, but 预算（万元） collapses into three stacked lines and 进度 breaks into short fragments, so the table grows ~40% taller than C/D for little gain in risk-text legibility."},"F":{"grade":"poor","why":"进度 is crushed to about two characters per line and 项目 to three, pushing the table to ~2981px; 风险说明 is widest here, but the cost to the progress and project columns outweighs it and the header block is fragmented."}},"best":["D"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"My pixel estimates of column widths are rough, especially for E and F where the render heights differ; C is a close second to D and could tie if the wrapped 预算 header is judged unimportant. I also cannot verify whether the 进度 column's short fragments are considered acceptable for this publication."}
